qualified_scope: cold task creation and cold-handle cleanup
single direct-await result claim after normal terminal publication
explicit .await? cancellation capture without a fabricated payload
detached result drain before default-runtime shutdown
known_behavior: After a direct await has claimed a normal child result, a later parent cancellation request preserves that normal claim; it does not suppress source-visible normal delivery.
unqualified_targets: cancel-join-drain across every await, TaskScope, race2, and select2 path
task-wide cleanup aggregation and structured-scope close progress
exact PlaceState/init/cede cleanup across await and terminal cancellation

proves: direct normal await claim is one-shot
a later cancellation request preserves the established normal claim

qualified_guarantees.statement: Creating an async task is cold: its body does not execute until activation.
Repeated activation does not create a second execution.
Dropping a cold handle reclaims its frame without running the task body.
Cold-drop cleanup discharges frame-owned cede parameters before canceled terminal publication or reclaim.
After normal terminal publication, direct await has exactly one normal-result claimant.
A later cancellation request preserves an already established direct normal-result claim.
At .await?, canceled child completion is represented as None and does not fabricate T.
Runtime-owned detached work drains its result obligation before block_on returns.
A task cancellation request is observable through the current bounded TaskHandle API.

operations.name: create
operations.handle_obligation: The caller owns the move-only TaskHandle until it is awaited, detached, or dropped.
operations.result_obligation: The promise result is pending and has no readable payload.
guarantees: Async function creation does not execute its body.

operations.name: activate
operations.handle_obligation: start, await, and wait may activate a created handle; repeated activation preserves state and cannot create a second execution.
operations.result_obligation: First activation leaves the result pending until terminal completion; repeated activation preserves the existing result state and cannot republish or reclaim it.
guarantees: start queues work and never inlines the task body on the caller stack.

operations.name: await
operations.handle_obligation: The direct awaiter is resumed exactly once after the child becomes terminal.
operations.result_obligation: After acquire-observing normal terminal completion, one claimant may privately claim and consume the ready-live result; canceled completion propagates cancellation and does not fabricate a payload.
guarantees: Completion before direct continuation registration remains linearized.
A normal child-result claim is one-shot and remains normal when a later cancellation request arrives.

operations.name: await-outcome
operations.handle_obligation: The direct awaiter is resumed exactly once after the child becomes terminal.
operations.result_obligation: After acquire-observing normal terminal completion, one claimant may privately claim and consume the ready-live result as Some(T); canceled completion is represented as None without fabricating T.
guarantees: Cancellation capture is explicit at the .await? boundary.
A normal child-result claim is one-shot and remains Some(T) when a later cancellation request arrives.

operations.name: cancel
operations.handle_obligation: Cancellation requests one observation epoch, wakes or queues suspended work, and may leave a running task running until its next observation boundary.
operations.result_obligation: Unhandled cancellation publishes canceled with no readable payload; explicit current-task cancellation capture may consume that request and later publish an ordinary normal result.
guarantees: A cancellation request is observable at the current task's cancellation boundary.
The .await? boundary consumes a captured current-task cancellation once and may continue to normal completion.

operations.name: drop
operations.handle_obligation: Dropping a created handle reclaims its frame; dropping an activated handle transfers runtime ownership through detach.
operations.result_obligation: Cold drop destroys frame-owned cede parameters without running the body and publishes canceled before reclaim; dropping activated or completed work transfers its result obligation to the bounded detached drain.
guarantees: Owner release is linearized exactly once.
Cold drop discharges every frame-owned no-body cleanup obligation before canceled terminal publication, completion notification, or reclaim.

operations.name: detach
operations.handle_obligation: The runtime owns an activated detached task until it reaches a terminal state.
operations.result_obligation: After acquire-observing normal terminal completion, a detached ready-live result is privately claimed once, destroyed through its compiler-installed typed drop entry, and published taken before frame reclamation; canceled completion has no payload.
guarantees: block_on drains runtime-owned detached work before executor shutdown.

result_states.name: pending
result_states.meaning: No normal payload ownership commit or canceled no-payload result has been published.

result_states.name: ready-live
result_states.meaning: A normal result payload has been committed, but no claimant may read or privately claim it until acquire-observing normal terminal completion; after that gate it permits exactly one typed transfer or destruction.

result_states.name: taken
result_states.meaning: The unique claimant completed typed transfer or destruction of the normal payload; it cannot be claimed again.

result_states.name: canceled
result_states.meaning: Cancellation completed without publishing a result payload.

proves: created drop does not execute the body
frame-owned cede parameter is reclaimed exactly once
runtime-owned detached work drains before block_on returns
detached frame local is dropped exactly once
current task cancellation can return a domain outcome
